title: Logging & Observability
outcome: Make production behavior observable with structured logs, request correlation, error monitoring, metrics, traces/signals, and actionable alerts.
artifact: Observability layer connecting Next.js/API errors and request IDs to structured logs and monitoring releases.
labSteps: Define the minimum structured fields every API request/error log should carry.
Generate or propagate a request ID and return it so support can correlate client reports.
Redact secrets and PII deliberately before adding rich context.
Integrate error monitoring for both Next.js and NestJS and tag releases by commit SHA.
Add a few meaningful application/HTTP/database signals rather than hundreds of vanity metrics.
Simulate a production-style error and walk from user-visible request ID to logs/monitoring evidence.
failureModes: console.log strings with no searchable structure
Alerts on every exception rather than user-impacting symptoms
No release/environment tags so errors cannot be tied to deployments
mastery: Can correlate one request across layers
principles: Logs should answer what happened, where, and for which request without exposing sensitive data.
Use request or correlation identifiers to connect events across application boundaries.
Metrics reveal system trends while traces and structured logs help explain individual failures.
Alert on user-impacting symptoms and actionable conditions rather than every noisy internal event.
